Article Title: 'Told them to give it to me in writing': Raihan Vadra recounts how events unfolded before photos were taken down at Bikaner House exhibition
Article Text:
Raihan Vadra alleges Bikaner House officials objected to protest photos, including those of Tricolour

Officials allegedly refused to provide written explanation

Dispute over photographs of the Tricolour

NEW DELHI: Artist and photographer Raihan Vadra, son of Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and businessman Robert Vadra, has detailed his interactions with Bikaner House officials over the removal of photographs depicting youth protests in Delhi from his exhibition, alleging that the administration gave him only a few hours to comply with its objections.Speaking about the controversy, Raihan said his solo exhibition, titled No Idea Is Fine, was scheduled to open at 7 pm, but the venue's management raised objections to some of the photographs shortly before the event.He alleged that officials subsequently insisted that all 70 images be removed, including photographs featuring the Indian national flag.Speaking to news agency ANI, Raihan said the Bikaner House management first contacted him 24 hours before the scheduled opening and told him that some images violated its policy. He said he asked the officials to identify the photographs and discuss their objections, but did not receive a response until the following day.He said the deputy resident commissioner later contacted him and instructed him to remove the photographs, which documented youth movements in Delhi over the preceding year.“I said, 'I shared the layout a week earlier; why didn't you bring it up earlier?' They said, 'We couldn't see the layout.'So I said, 'You still had 1 week to tell me you couldn't see the layout. I would have sent it; we could have had the discussion earlier. Now, in 4-5 hours, what am I going to do?'” Raihan said.Raihan said he asked the management to provide written explanations for the removal of individual photographs but did not receive them.He said the principal resident commissioner subsequently visited the exhibition at around 3 pm and reiterated the objections. According to Raihan, the official cited the venue's policy against political content.Raihan said he had already removed most photographs featuring political parties and leaders and was willing to replace any remaining images that violated the policy.“For the most part, I had removed imagery of political parties and of political leaders. Maybe there were a few photographs; I said, 'We could discuss. If they are against your policy, I'll replace them.' He said, 'No, none of these 70 images will be put up,'” he said.According to Raihan, the management issued a notice at 3.30 pm warning that the building would be sealed and the exhibition cancelled if the photographs were not removed by 5 pm.He said he initially complied by turning the framed photographs around so that only their backs were visible. However, he alleged that officials objected to this arrangement as well, prompting him to take the frames down and move them into storage.Raihan said he left two photographs featuring the Indian flag on display, arguing that they could not reasonably violate the venue's policy. He alleged that officials asked him to remove them but did not provide a written order when he requested one.“I said, 'This can't be against your policy. How can it be against your policy?' I said, 'Give it to me in writing that you want me to take down a picture of the Indian flag.' They didn't,” he said.Raihan added that he left the venue to change clothes and that officials removed one of the two photographs themselves. One image of the national flag remained on display, he said.In an earlier statement, Raihan had said he would not remove the photographs featuring the Tricolour and that the exhibition would proceed in a limited capacity while he looked for an alternative venue to display the complete collection.The controversy drew reactions from members of the Congress. Priyanka Gandhi Vadra backed her son in a post on X, writing, “When someone with power becomes afraid of the expression of another, he doesn’t know it, but he has already lost the very power he is trying to protect. You stand for what is true and everything beautiful will find its way to you. I am proud of you, always will be.”Robert Vadra also shared his son's statement, while Congress MP Karti Chidambaram criticised the Bikaner House administration's conduct.Congress Rajya Sabha MP Pawan Khera alleged that the removal of the photographs amounted to censorship.In a post on X, he said the works documented protests and questioned why images of demonstrations, including the national flag, had become objectionable.The exhibition, No Idea Is Fine, was scheduled to open at Bikaner House on Thursday evening.
Article Summary: Raihan Vadra alleges Bikaner House officials objected to protest photos, including those of the Tricolour.Officials allegedly refused to provide written explanation for the removal of the images. Priyanka Gandhi Vadra backed her son in a post on X.

Article Title: 'Tricolor row': What happened at Priyanka Gandhi’s son Raihan’s exhibition at Bikaner House - controversy explained
Article Text:
Artist and Photographer Raihan Vadra, son of Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, with one of his photographs at Bikaner House, in New Delhi. (PTI Photo)

Why were the photographs removed

Priyanka Gandhi, Congress leaders react

NEW DELHI: A controversy erupted at Delhi’s Bikaner House after artist and photographer Raihan Vadra, son of Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and businessman Robert Vadra, alleged that the venue’s management asked him to remove around 74 photographs documenting recent youth protests ahead of his solo exhibition, “No Idea Is Final”.Raihan also alleged that he was asked to remove two photographs of the Indian flag, saying he had refused to take them down.The exhibition opened as scheduled on Wednesday, with around 40 photographs remaining on display while more than 70 were removed, according to a PTI report. The show, featuring wildlife photography, abstract works and images of recent youth movements, is scheduled to continue until Sunday.In a post on Instagram, Raihan wrote, "Five hours ago, the Bikaner House Management forced me to remove the bulk of the artworks displayed in my show "No Idea Is Final", which opens this evening at 7 pm. The photos were of the youth protests in Delhi. Apparently, the content is "objectionable". They also directed me to remove two photos of the Tiranga. I have refused. I will not take down a picture of the Indian flag."Raihan told PTI that the management had raised objections to the “political nature” of the protest photographs. He said he was informed at 3.30 pm on Wednesday that the images had to be removed by 5 pm or the exhibition would be cancelled.According to Raihan, the management said that, given the prevailing political climate in India, it was not the right time to display the images. He maintained that the photographs did not convey a political message and merely documented protests over the preceding six months."I felt it is my duty as an Indian artist, not just because I am doing a show right now, but it is my duty as an Indian artist to document what is going on... They are censoring the work of artists, I don't know what they are scared of. They even went to the extent of removing the picture of the Indian flag," he told PTI.Raihan also said he had shared the exhibition proposal and layout with the management well in advance and objected to the removal of nearly half the artworks less than 24 hours before the opening.A Bikaner House official told PTI that the administration was not authorised to comment on the matter.Priyanka Gandhi Vadra criticised the alleged removal of the photographs, describing it as an attempt to silence young voices."I think it's ridiculous. What do you think? He is a young boy but I suppose you know, they are muzzling the voice of the youth across the nation. So it's only expected that they'll do it to anyone," she told PTI."His photographs of the protests, not a single commentary, not a single thing that was either derogatory towards anyone, just a visual documentation of the protest. So, I mean, clearly this is the way they think. It's not a democracy anymore. Today it's him, tomorrow it'll be another artist," she added.Senior Congress leader Pawan Khera also criticised the alleged censorship, questioning why photographs documenting protests had been considered objectionable."When even the Tricolour isn’t safe from the censor’s scissors, perhaps the problem isn’t the art. It’s the regime. Just hours before @raihanrvadra was to open his art show ‘No Idea Is Final ’, 74 artworks - nearly half the exhibition - were taken down for being 'political ' by the Bikaner House. The photographs merely documented protests, and not one was derogatory or inflammatory. So what exactly was the offence?" he said.Khera further alleged that a photograph of the Tricolour was among the works Raihan had to fight to retain. Congress MP Karti Chidambaram also condemned the alleged censorship, calling the administration's behaviour "obtuse" and "churlish."The Indian Youth Congress Legal Cell also reacted to the controversy, posting on X: "IYC Legal Cell's tweet: YOU CAN CENSOR THE FRAME. NOT THE TRUTH. Saheb dara hua hai (sir is scared)."Raihan said the exhibition would continue with the works still on display and indicated that he could seek another venue if necessary to show the full collection of protest photographs.
Article Summary: Photographer Raihan Vadra, son of Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi, says he was asked to remove 74 photographs of recent youth protests. He claims he was told the images had to be removed by 5 pm or the exhibition would be cancelled. The exhibition opened as scheduled on Wednesday with around 40 photographs remaining on display while more than 70 were removed.

Article Title: ‘Finding a place to belong’: Sonia Gandhi makes Instagram debut, shares first look of memoir
Article Text:
Sonia Gandhi joins Instagram, shares first look of memoir ‘Belonging: A Journey of Love’

Memoir revisits childhood, Rajiv Gandhi and family tragedies

India edition faces publishing uncertainty

NEW DELHI: Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi joined Instagram on Thursday and shared the first look of her upcoming memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, which is scheduled for release on November 10.In her first post on the social media platform, the 79-year-old Congress leader expressed gratitude while introducing the book to readers.“Hello everyone, I’m truly grateful to share this moment with you all; the first look of Belonging: A Journey of Love,” she wrote in the caption.“It is a story of love, duty, loss and finding a place to belong. I look forward to sharing it with you,” the post added.The memoir traces Congress MP’s journey from her childhood in post-war Italy to her relationship with former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi and the personal losses that shaped her life and relationship with India.The book recounts Sonia’s early years in Italy, her romance with Rajiv Gandhi while they were associated with Cambridge, and the assassinations of her mother-in-law, former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, and her husband.Born in Italy, Sonia Gandhi was 19 when she met Rajiv Gandhi in Cambridge, England, in 1965. The couple married on February 25, 1968.She went on to become the longest-serving president of the Congress party.Her memoir is expected to offer a personal account of love, identity, duty and belonging, alongside her experiences as a member of the Nehru-Gandhi family and her life in India.Rahul Gandhi had earlier expressed excitement about the book. On the 82nd birth anniversary of his father, Rajiv Gandhi, the leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha wrote that he was proud his mother’s story would reach readers.“I am happy, and so proud, that your story--'Belonging: A Journey of Love'--will finally be read by the millions of people who love you. I know how hard it was for someone as private as you to tell the world your beautiful story. Today, on his birthday, I can see Papa smiling and looking down proudly at his beautiful Sonia,” Rahul Gandhi said.The memoir is scheduled to be published internationally by Alfred A Knopf, an imprint of the Knopf Doubleday Publishing Group, on November 10. The announcement was made on August 18.However, the book’s publication in India has faced uncertainty following a disagreement between Penguin Random House India (PRHI) and the author’s representatives over editorial changes.Penguin India said the publication process had reached an “impasse over a particular issue” during its normal editorial review. The publisher said some proposed changes had been accepted, while in other instances it had accepted the author’s position, but an agreement could not be reached on one issue.Penguin India denied that external pressure had influenced the decision and declined to disclose details of the disagreement, citing contractual obligations and author confidentiality.The dispute triggered a political controversy, with Congress leaders alleging that pressure had been exerted to remove sections concerning Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and China’s occupation of Indian territory during the Modi government.Former Rajasthan chief minister Ashok Gehlot described the episode as a “murder of democracy”.Penguin India rejected suggestions of external intervention, saying its review involved the usual editorial processes, including fact-checking and recommendations.Later, HarperCollins India had stepped in to publish the domestic edition, with the book expected to reach Indian readers on the same date as its international release.The status of the India edition had remained a point of contention following Penguin India’s exit from the deal.Former Congress president’s Instagram debut comes ahead of the memoir’s scheduled release, offering readers an early glimpse of the book and its account of her personal journey.
Article Summary: Sonia Gandhi joins Instagram, shares first look of memoir ‘Belonging: A Journey of Love’Memoir revisits childhood, Rajiv Gandhi and family tragedies.India edition faces publishing uncertainty following disagreement with Penguin Random House India.

Article Title: 'Shouldn't have come if unwell': Subodh Uniyal defends public reprimand of Daler Mehndi
Article Text:
Congress demands minister's apology

Artists rally behind Mehndi

NEW DELHI: Uttarakhand minister Subodh Uniyal on Wednesday defended himself over reprimanding singer Daler Mehndi on stage during an event, saying the artiste should not have performed if he was unwell.Speaking to news agency PTI, Uniyal said Mehndi was only lip-syncing during the event and that, as a public representative associated with the event's organising committee, he came under pressure from people who wanted the issue to be questioned."Daler Mehndi, being a big name, was invited to the Kunjapuri Fair. But during the performance, it became apparent that he was only lip-syncing and not singing. I, being a local representative and also associated with the organising committee, felt the pressure from people who wanted this to be questioned," Uniyal said."Mehndi was not able to speak or walk. At that point, I thought he was under the influence of some substance. I don't know what, because a medical examination was not conducted," he added.Uniyal said he later learnt that Mehndi was unable to speak because he was unwell."Being such a big artiste, he should have informed us about this. This fact was revealed only when he was interrupted. If he was unwell, he should not have come to perform," the minister said."We were asked to make full payment of Rs 35 lakh in advance to the artiste; hotels were also booked in advance. I have nothing personal against Mehndi nor any intention to hurt him, but such a big artiste, knowing his condition, should have refused to perform," Uniyal said."I stand by the fact that if an artiste's respect must stay intact, they should also work accordingly. I did not use any foul language while speaking to Mehndi," he added.The controversy erupted after Uniyal went on stage and expressed displeasure while Mehndi was performing at the Siddhpeeth Maa Kunjapuri Tourism and Development Fair, a cultural event organised by the Uttarakhand government at Narendra Nagar in the New Tehri area on Sunday night.The controversy also took on political overtones, with Congress demanding that Uniyal publicly apologise for the way the episode was handled.“The treatment meted out to Mehndi is deeply unfortunate and runs counter to Uttarakhand’s glorious tradition of hospitality,” Amarjit Singh, general secretary of the Uttarakhand Pradesh Congress Committee, said.Meanwhile, several people from the entertainment industry, including actor Anupam Kher, stand-up comedian Vir Das and singers Shaan, Palash Sen, Gurdas Maan and Alisha Chinai, came out in support of Mehndi. They said the artiste, who has been singing for three decades, was unwell, did not drink and should have been treated with greater respect."Couple of days ago, I saw a video in which Daler Mehndi ji was singing on stage and some minister got up and spoke to him insultingly. I wasn't there so I don't know but I've known Daler ji for 25 to 30 years. I know that he does not drink and he is one of the finest human beings that I have met. I personally know that he has not been keeping well for two-three years," Kher said in a video on X on Wednesday."Nobody should speak to anybody like this and that also on a public forum. This is not fair. To publicly accuse someone like this is wrong. Daler ji I am so sorry," he added.Comedian Vir Das said his first international show was in Dubai at Mehndi's show."So not just music people, comedy people also have a lot to owe to this great man and this great artist. And he was humble, nice, supportive and amazing. Daler paaji, I hope you feel well in your corner. Thank you from a very young comedian," Das said on Instagram.Mehndi's brother, singer Mika Singh, confirmed that the artiste had undergone major surgery and challenged anyone to prove that his elder brother had ever consumed alcohol. Although there has been speculation about Mehndi's health, the nature of his illness and surgery remains unclear.FWICE (Federation of Western India Cine Employees) also wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami over alleged public humiliation of the singer.
Article Summary: Uttarakhand minister Subodh Uniyal defends himself over reprimanding singer Daler Mehndi on stage during an event. He says the artiste should not have performed if he was unwell. Congress demands minister's apology for the way the episode was handled. Several people from the entertainment industry, including actor Anupam Kher, stand-up comedian Vir Das and singers Shaan, Palash Sen, Gurdas Maan and Alisha Chinai, came out in support of Meh second.

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janata Party leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka walked out of Tihar Jail after on Wednesday after 7 days of judicial custody.Their release was ordered after a special executive magistrate (SEM) court in Delhi accepted the surety bonds. The both were seen smiling as they got into their car as Ranka said "Inquilab Zindabad".Meanwhile, earlier on their way back fromt he police station to Tihar Jail after the release ordert was given, Das in a brief interaction with media responded saying, "Truth has triumphed."The CJP founder and leader Abhijeet Dipke shared his reaction to the court's release order. Taking to his X account, Dipke shared a clip from the climax scene of Shah Rukh Khan's movie Chak De India. Later called Das and Ranka "much better" than him. "Saurav and Ashu are not just better but much much bigger leaders than me," he said on X. "Happy to follow your orders my leaders. Jaan hazir hai! Lekin iske baad mere bina garden me koi akela nahi ghumega!!!" he added.Earlier in the day, Das andRanka approached the Delhi high court challenging the extension of their custody following a protest at Jantar Mantar. The court questioned why they had invoked its writ jurisdiction when an alternative legal remedy was available.“Your second incident. You are a person who has actually broken a bond. Your remedy actually lies in revision,” the court observed. It also raised concerns that breaching barricades could encourage others to violate prohibitory orders.“When you go and break a barricade, the chances of 10 or 20 more people in violation of 163 are very high,” the court said. The petitioners argued that the Sub-Divisional Executive Magistrate (SEM) lacked jurisdiction to extend their custody and had wrongly rejected their sureties. The court asked them to await the SEM's decision and pursue the appropriate legal remedy if necessary, following which they withdrew their plea. The bench clarified that it had expressed no opinion on the merits of the case.

Article Title: ‘Then, you are not Gen Z?’ Delhi High Court’s light-hearted exchange with CJP leaders; Dipke reacts
Article Text:
File photo: CJP leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das & Ashutosh Ranka

Court questions choice of legal remedy

Petition withdrawn

NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court had a light-hearted exchange during a hearing on Wednesday involving Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, with Justice Subramonium Prasad remarking that the two were not part of Generation Z after being told their ages.During the hearing, Justice Prasad asked advocate Abhik Chimni, appearing for the petitioners, how old the two leaders were. Chimni told the court that Das was 27 and Ranka was 32.“Then you are not Gen Z. What is Gen Z?” the court asked.After being informed that Generation Z generally refers to people born after 1997, the court reiterated, “Then you are not Gen Z.”The exchange took place while the high court was hearing the leaders’ challenge to an October 19 order by a Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) extending their judicial custody until October 21.The exchange also drew a reaction on social media, with CJP leader Abhijit Dipke posting an image of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and writing, “The only person who qualifies as GenZ.”During the hearing, the court questioned why the petitioners had approached it under Article 226 of the Constitution when an alternative remedy of revision could be available to challenge the magistrate’s order.“Your second incident. You are a person who has actually broken a bond.Your remedy actually lies in revision,” the court observed.The bench also questioned whether the authorities could insist on stricter surety conditions following an alleged second breach of a peace bond.“Once you have broken peace for the second time, are the authorities not entitled to insist upon everything?” the court asked.The court further noted that a challenge to the denotification of Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site was pending before the Supreme Court and that the notification had not been stayed. It questioned the petitioners’ decision to return to the site in those circumstances.The bench also expressed concern that breaking barricades could encourage others to violate prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS).“The two petitioners here are at the forefront. When you go and break a barricade, the chances of 10 or 20 more people in violation of 163 are very high,” the court observed.Advocate Chimni argued that the SEM's October 19 order extending the petitioners' custody was legally unsustainable. He contended that the magistrate lacked jurisdiction to extend their custody and alleged that preventive proceedings were being used arbitrarily.He also questioned the rejection of the sureties, arguing that two additional sureties were available but had not been called for consideration.According to his submissions, the magistrate's order referred to discrepancies in photographs and difficulties in verifying details relating to one of the petitioners.The court suggested that the petitioners await the outcome of proceedings before the SEM, which was scheduled to reconsider their sureties at 2 pm on Wednesday. Chimni, however, expressed apprehension that the sureties could again be rejected on fresh grounds, requiring the petitioners to approach the High Court again.The petitioners subsequently withdrew their plea. Justice Prasad permitted the withdrawal, and the High Court clarified that it had not expressed any opinion on the merits of the case.Additional solicitor general Chetan Sharma, along with advocate Ashish Dixit, appeared for the Delhi Police, while Chimni represented Das, Ranka and the other petitioners.
Article Summary: The Delhi High Court had a light-hearted exchange during a hearing on Wednesday involving Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. Justice Subramonium Prasad remarked that the two were not part of Generation Z after being told their ages.

Article Title: 7,000 people from 126 districts once hit by Naxalism to attend Ekta Diwas parade in Kevadia
Article Text:
Rashtriya Ekta Diwas 2026 to celebrate 'End of Naxalism': Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The end of armed Naxalism within the March 31, 2026 deadline set by home minister Amit Shah as well 150 years of ‘Vande Mataram’ will be celebrated at the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas parade and Bharat Parv at Kevadia, Gujarat, this year to mark Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel’s birth anniversary on Oct 31. Around 7,000 people from 126 districts that at some point of time were under the scourge of Left-wing extremism, will participate both as performers and spectators in the event to be graced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi Union home secretary Govind Mohan on Wednesday said around 2,000 artists drawn from 126 districts that were once Naxal-affected, will join the celebrations by putting up a dramatic performance, directed by the National School of Drama (NSD), through which they will recount how their life and property were threatened when Naxalism was rampant in their area.In addition, around 5,000 local people from these 126 districts have been invited. They will not only be spectators for all the performances but will also, through their interactions, share the hardships they had to undergo at the hands of Maoists and how their lives have changed now.“Their participation will underline the resilience of communities that have endured conflict and highlight the role of cultural expression in strengthening national integration,” said Govind Mohan.The 2026 edition of the parade will also feature march-past by contingents of all the central armed police forces (CAPFs) and state police personnel who were in the forefront of the decisive fight against left-wing extremist violence. A short film will play on LED screens at the venue as the contingents pass in front of the Prime Minister, the chief guest, summarising the salient feature of their achievements in eliminating armed Naxalism.The three elements (marchpast, drama, interactions), the home secretary said, will showcase India’s struggle against armed Naxalism, the fact it has now been eradicated and most importantly, how development has replaced violence in the affected districts.The Ekta Diwas parade, to be held in the evening hours this year, will also feature tableaux designed around the theme of “Vande Mataram” and constructed by the people and private entities with corporate social responsibility (CSR) funds, with no involvement of the govt. The 15 designs for the tableaux, selected through competition, are based on the implications of ‘Vande Mataram’ on nationhood and development.There will also be a cultural programme curated entirely by people from different states and communities who have made Gujarat their home. Around 5,000 artists will showcase dances and culture of their respective states through this mega-performance.A play will be organised on the eve of Oct 31 on the theme ‘Anand Math’. To be directed by NSD, it will be based on the abiding philosophy of Anand Math: that every person of India has a responsibility of building a bright future for the country and being aware of its cultural heritage.
Article Summary: The end of armed Naxalism within the March 31, 2026 deadline set by home minister Amit Shah will be celebrated at the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas parade and Bharat Parv at Kevadia, Gujarat. Around 7,000 people from 126 districts that at some point of time were under the scourge of Left-wing extremism, will participate both as performers and spectators.

Article Title: Ankita Bhandari case: CBI serves notice to actress Urmila Sanawar for narco test
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on Wednesday served actress Urmila Sanawar a notice asking her to appear before a court in Dehradun on October 23 to give her consent for polygraph and narco-analysis tests in connection with the Ankita Bhandari murder case.Sanawar said a CBI team visited her residence on Wednesday, after questioning her for around four hours on October 18."The CBI questioned me on the 18th. Today, I received a call from a CBI officer asking if I was at home. Upon arriving at my residence, they served me a notice for a narco-analysis test and asked me to appear before them the day after tomorrow at 10:30 AM," she said."This notice is related to the audio clip that went viral in the Ankita Bhandari murder case," Sanawar told ANI.According to the notice, Sanawar has been directed to appear before the designated court on October 23, 2026, at 10:30am to ascertain whether she is willing to undergo the tests voluntarily."Now, therefore, you are hereby directed to appear in person before this Court on 23/10/2026 at 10:30 AM for the purpose of ascertaining whether you are willing to undergo the proposed Polygraph Test and Narco Test (Lie detection Tests) examination voluntarily and without any coercion, undue influence, threat, inducement or pressure from any person or authority," the notice stated.The development comes amid a controversy over the alleged involvement of a "VIP" in the September 2022 murder of Ankita Bhandari, a receptionist at a resort near Rishikesh in Uttarakhand.The row has intensified following the appointment of former BJP Uttarakhand in-charge Dushyant Gautam as the governor of Sikkim.Earlier this month, a four-member CBI team visited Sanawar's residence in Saharanpur as part of the investigation.On Saturday, the agency also questioned former Uttarakhand BJP MLA Suresh Rathore at his residence.Speaking to reporters in Haridwar, Rathore said, "I cooperated with the investigation - nothing more, nothing less. I have no further comment. I have no further comment. NEW DELHI: The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has asked Alliance Air to “strengthen simulator training requirements for flight crew by incorporating advanced scenarios involving heavy rain, low-visibility approaches, and rapidly deteriorating weather conditions. ” This recommendation has been made in the final report of a serious incident on Oct 8, 2024, when an Alliance ATR (VT-RKF) with 47 people on board had undershot the runway at Bhubaneswar during landing in “severe” rain.It had “made ground contact approximately 100 metres before the runway threshold.” Luckily there were no injuries to the 43 passengers and four crew members. Also there was no fire on the aircraft which had flown in from Rourkela.“Inadequate communication, cross-checking, mutual intervention, and challenge-response coordination between the pilots contributed to the ineffective management of deteriorating approach conditions and the failure to initiate a timely go-Around. After landing, the pilot-in-command informed ATC that the aircraft had landed on Runway 51 instead of Runway 14, possibly due to nervousness, stress, and confusion following the serious incident, indicating a temporary lapse in situational awareness,” says the report.AAIB has listed these among the contributory factors: “Severe convective weather conditions include heavy rain, turbulence, downdrafts, and low visibility in the runway environment. Presence of significant low-level wind shear characterised by rapid transition from headwind to tailwind close to the ground.”AAIB has recommended that Alliance Air should place “special emphasis on pilots who have recorded operational exceedances within a six-month period, with mandatory recurrent simulator sessions and targeted remedial training to enhance decision-making, situational awareness, and adherence to standard operating procedures during adverse weather operations.”

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Article Title: 'Told he was murdered by a fellow athlete': Preeti Pal, India's Asian Para Games medallist, recalls losing training partner earlier this year

India’s Preeti Pal dedicated her second silver medal at the Asian Para Games to her training partner Chirag Tyagi, who was shot dead in May. The sprinter remembered Chirag as a younger brother who dreamed of winning medals for India. She believes he would have reached the podium in Nagoya, Japan, had he been alive.Preeti and fellow Indian sprinter Simran Sharma trained with Chirag at Delhi’s Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium under coach Gajendra Singh. His death left both athletes devastated, and memories of him returned as they celebrated their achievements at the Games.“Within a short time, Chirag became our trusted training partner. He was like a younger brother, but he guided us,” Preeti told The Indian Express.She recalled Chirag’s ambition to represent India on the international stage. “I still remember him telling me, ‘Preeti didi, ek din main bhi apki aur Simran didi ki tarah Paralympic aur Asian Games main medal jeetunga aur tirange ko rise hote dekhunga (One day I too will win medals for India in Paralympics and Asian Games and watch the Indian tricolour rise high).’ I dedicate the medals I won to Chirag. He was like a younger brother,” she said.Preeti, who has cerebral palsy, won silver in the women’s 100m T35 final in 13.98 seconds on Wednesday, adding to her silver in the 200m T35 event on Tuesday.Simran, who has impaired vision, won her second gold medal of the Games by claiming the women’s 100m T12 title in an Asian Para Games record time of 12.02 seconds, following her 200m gold.Preeti recalled how she first learned of Chirag’s death while visiting her family in Uttar Pradesh.“Initially, we thought it was an accident. Some hours later, we were told that Chirag was murdered by a fellow athlete. It was a tough phase for us. Chirag stayed in the room opposite us at the stadium. When we are at the stadium, we are reminded of him every day,” she said.Chirag’s parents, Manoj and Nisha, followed the athletes’ performances from home.His mother said he was inspired by Preeti and Simran and was proud of their achievements. Both athletes, along with their coach, have also stayed in touch with the family and provided financial support.Chirag had qualified for the Para Asian Games in the men’s 400m and 1500m T12 events after winning gold at the Indian Open Para Athletics International Championship in Bengaluru in May.Preeti remembered how Chirag had cheered her on when she won the 100m T35 title at the World Para Athletics Championships in New Delhi last year.“We had a deep bond,” she said, adding that she regretted never tying a rakhi on his wrist. “Winning medals gives me joy. I wish Chirag were with us to share the joy.”

NEW DELHI: Para-cyclist Shaik Arshad suffered multiple fractures to his previously operated left residual limb after a fall during the men’s time trial at the Asian Para Games in Japan on Wednesday, raising questions over the absence of dedicated medical support for the Indian team.Sources told TOI that Arshad, a 2024 Paralympian, crashed in heavy rain at the Izu Velodrome in Shizuoka, sustaining serious injuries to the above-knee amputated limb on which he relies to use his prosthesis. He requires urgent medical attention and surgery, with concerns over the implications for his future mobility.The cycling venue is more than 250 km from Nagoya. Sources said officials had initially asked Arshad and his support staff to travel to Nagoya for hospital admission. Following prolonged discussions, officials agreed to visit the competition venue, where the injured cyclist needed immediate attention.The incident has also raised questions about assurances regarding medical arrangements for the Indian para-cycling contingent. Sources said that at a meeting on Sept 8 at the Sports Authority of India (SAI) office here, involving Arshad’s coach Aditya Verma and SAI officials from the Teams division, with Paralympic Committee of India (PCI) officials participating through phone calls, assurances were apparently given that medical personnel would accompany the team.However, no dedicated medical personnel were available to attend to Arshad at the venue when the accident occurred, sources alleged. Arshad’s coach is now exploring options to travel urgently from Hyderabad to Japan and is arranging a visa to be by the athlete’s side.The injury is particularly serious because it involves Arshad’s residual limb, which is crucial for fitting and using his artificial leg. The extent of the fractures and the treatment required will determine the impact on his recovery and mobility.

Suvarna Raj's work beyond sports

What is the F54 discus throw category?

Suvarna Raj, a 44-year-old para-athlete from Greater Noida, won gold for India in the women's F54 discus throw at the Asian Para Games on Thursday. She finished first with a best throw of 15.66m, adding another medal to her international career.A wheelchair user, Suvarna has been competing in para-athletics since 2017. She has represented India at three Asian Para Games and several international events. Away from sports, she works to improve accessibility for people with disabilities.Suvarna produced a steady performance in the final, with four of her six throws going beyond 15m. Her best effort came in the fifth attempt, when she threw 15.66m to take the gold medal.Iran's Shahla Hadidi won silver with 15.45m, while Vietnam's Thi Ngoc Thuy Nguyen finished third with 14.65m.Suvarna's six attempts were 13.68m, 15.09m, 15.05m, 14.57m, 15.66m and 15.19m.Suvarna is an international para-athlete who competes in the F54 discus throw category. She is coached by Pintu Nagar and has built her career through regular training and hard work since taking up the sport in 2017.She is ranked second in Asia in the F54 discus throw, according to previously reported rankings.Her latest gold at the Asian Para Games adds to a growing list of achievements.Suvarna has won medals at several international competitions.Suvarna is also an accessibility specialist and disability rights advocate. She has carried out more than 1,000 accessibility audits across India to help identify barriers faced by people with disabilities.She has also served as the Election Commission of India's Brand Ambassador for Accessible Elections, supporting efforts to make voting easier for people with disabilities.Her training and competition expenses are supported under the government's Annual Calendar for Training and Competition (ACTC). She has received financial assistance of Rs 7,70,607 under the programme.F54 is a classification for seated field athletes whose impairments affect trunk and lower-body function. Athletes compete from a throwing chair and use their arms and upper-body strength to throw the discus.Limited trunk control can affect how they balance and generate power during a throw.

Article Title: Priyanka Gandhi’s son Raihan Vadra's photos of protest taken down by Bikaner House
Article Text:
Raihan Vadra, an artist, faced issues at Bikaner House regarding his exhibition's protest images





NEW DELHI: Artist and photographer Raihan Vadra, son of Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and businessman Robert Vadra, has alleged that the Bikaner House administration removed several photographs documenting recent protests and youth movements in India, just hours before the opening of his solo exhibition.Titled No Idea is Final, the exhibition was previewed on Wednesday and is scheduled to open on Thursday.Speaking to news agency PTI, Raihan said the administration gave him a deadline to remove the photographs, warning that the exhibition would otherwise be cancelled.“They told us at 3.30 pm today if the images are not taken down by 5 pm, the show will be cancelled. They said it is not the right time for such photos to be shown,” he said.Raihan also alleged that an image of the national flag was taken down by the administration, but he subsequently put it back.In a statement shared with PTI, Raihan said the exhibition featured a mix of wildlife photography, abstract works and street photography documenting recent youth movements in India.He said the Bikaner House management had first contacted him at 6 pm on Tuesday, raising objections to what it described as the “political nature” of the protest photographs and asking him to remove them.Raihan objected to the timing of the request, saying he had shared the exhibition’s detailed proposal and layout with the management well in advance.“I made it clear that in view of the fact that I had shared the detailed proposal and layout of the show well in advance with the Bikaner House management it was incorrect on their part to request the removal of 50% of the artworks less than 24 hours before the opening,” he said.The Bikaner House administration was not immediately available for comment on the allegations.

Article Title: CJP activists’ detention puts spotlight on how SEMs play a crucial role
Article Text:
Recent observations by the Delhi HC have scrutinized the actions of these magistrates concerning the detainment of CJP activists

Who are SEMs?

How are they different from judicial magistrates?

When can an SEM ask someone to furnish a peace bond ?

Procedure: Under Section 130, the magistrate must issue a written order explaining the basis for the proceedings, the proposed bond amount, its duration and the number of sureties required.

Duration: A peace bond can be required for up to one year, and the amount must not be excessive.

Can it be challenged? The person must be given an opportunity to explain why they should not be required to furnish the bond. The magistrate then conducts an inquiry under Section 135.

When can an SEM order detention?

During inquiry: Under Section 135(3), an SEM may require immediate security if necessary to prevent a breach of peace or danger to public safety. If the person fails to furnish it, they may be detained until the inquiry concludes.

After inquiry: Under Section 136, the magistrate can order security if the inquiry establishes it is necessary. Under Section 137, the person must be discharged if the need for security isn’t established.

Failure to furnish security: Section 141 provides for imprisonment in specified circumstances, including failure to furnish security after a final order or breach of a qualifying bond.

Who can stand as a surety?

“Photograph mismatch”: The first surety’s photograph on the bond allegedly didn’t match his Aadhaar

“Insufficient identity proof”: He reportedly failed to produce another valid ID and gave unsatisfactory answers during questioning

“Lack of basic details”: The second surety couldn’t provide basic information, including the parentage and address of Saurav Das, for whom she stood as surety

“Insufficient control”: The SEM concluded the sureties didn’t have sufficient control over the activists to ensure their presence when required





NEW DELHI: Though a common feature in cases involving summary or preventive detention by police, the powers of special executive magistrates (SEMs) have come into focus due to their prominent role in deciding if those involved in recent protests rocking Delhi are released or remain behind bars.A person not familiar with the rare, overlapping functions and powers of the executive and judiciary may conclude SEMs are a rung of the judiciary where a person picked up by police is produced within 24 hours.However, the reality is more complex, since the law empowers govt officials, mostly police officers, to exercise magisterial powers in cases of detention, where they can even remand a detainee to judicial custody, as happened in the case of CJP’s Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka.Wednesday was the first time decisions taken by SEMs came under judicial scrutiny of any kind, when Delhi HC heard the CJP members’ plea. The court, however, refused to go into merits.Under Section 15 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), state govts can appoint executive magistrates or police officers of at least superintendent of police rank as SEMs for specific areas, periods or duties.Depending on state-specific notifications, these officers can also be deputy collectors or tehsildars or senior police officers of ACP rank.Their primary role is to take preventive measures to maintain public order and stop anticipated breaches of peace.Under BNSS Section 9, the state govt establishes courts of judicial magistrates in consultation with HC, which appoints their presiding officers. Judicial magistrates deal with criminal cases and trials while SEMs exercise executive powers, including initiating preventive proceedings.SEMs cannot conduct criminal trials or convict people through these proceedings, but are authorised to release or grant police or judicial remand. Under the earlier Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), the corresponding provision for SEMs was Section 21.Under Section 126, an SEM can initiate proceedings if there is sufficient ground to believe a person is likely to breach the peace or disturb public tranquillity.Separately, Section 163 allows an executive magistrate to issue urgent orders to prevent specified dangers or disturbances, including restricting public gatherings when legal conditions are met.Detention is not automatic once proceedings begin.A surety undertakes responsibility under a bond to help ensure the person concerned meets its conditions. Under Section 140, an SEM can reject a surety found unfit, but must conduct an inquiry, give the parties a reasonable opportunity to be heard and record reasons in writing.In Das and Ranka’s case, the SEM rejected fresh sureties over reported “discrepancies” in identification documents and missing details.
Article Summary: The powers of special executive magistrates (SEMs) have come into focus due to their prominent role in deciding if those involved in recent protests are released or remain behind bars. Wednesday was the first time decisions taken by SEMs came under judicial scrutiny of any kind, when Delhi HC heard the CJP members’ plea.

Article Title: 'I clean, they dirty faster': MP's Bittu Tabahi may quit cleaning river forever
Article Text:
Photo: @bittu_tabahi/ Instagram

Bittu cleaned river stretch alone, larger civic failure is now making him fight losing battle





BHOPAL: Madhya Pradesh's 20-year-old college student Surendra Singh Choudhary-better known to the country as "Bittu Tabahi"-is a dejected man. Bittu, who hogged international limelight for single-handedly cleaning up a stretch of Ajnar river in Rajgarh's Biaora, says every time he cleans up the river, people dump garbage back into it-sometimes almost immediately. The situation worsened after Dussehra, when fresh waste accumulated along the banks he had worked so hard to restore."I have been working to clean this river for the past year. Every time I have cleaned it, people have dirtied it again," he said, his voice heavy with disappointment. "I am starting to lose heart.""I think I should focus on my studies," Bittu said.I don't believe I will be able to continue cleaning the Ajnar river any longer."The statement marks a troubling turn for a campaign that became a symbol of individual environmental action. Bittu's central argument remains simple: removing garbage is only temporary if people continue to throw waste into the river. Lasting change, he believes, requires citizens to stop littering in the first place.Ajnar, which flows through Biaora in Rajgarh district, had long been treated as an open dumping ground.Passers-by reportedly covered their mouths with cloth to escape its stench. Bittu began cleaning a stretch of the river on Jan 26, initially with a few friends, but soon found himself working alone, armed with little more than basic tools and determination.There was no govt order, no funding and no formal campaign behind his effort. He used his own money for supplies, entered foul water despite not knowing how to swim, and removed waste bag by bag. For a while, the results were visible. The stretch Bittu cleaned became noticeably clearer, and his videos earned praise from across India and abroad.But that recognition has not stopped the river from being littered again. His frustration deepened after he installed two dustbins along the riverbank, hoping residents and visitors would dispose of waste responsibly. One of the bins later went missing. Bittu clarified that the dustbins were meant for public use, not personal convenience.During another clean-up, conducted with the local Nagar Palika team, Bittu found an Indian national flag among the waste. He used the moment to ask a question that has become central to his campaign: "When will we understand our responsibility?"Those who have followed Bittu's work describe a young volunteer whose energy was once extraordinary. He cleaned without machinery, faced health risks and snake encounters, and continued even after criticism. But repeated relapse of pollution has begun to test that resolve. Bittu's exhaustion highlights a larger civic failure. A single student can clean a river, but he cannot police a town's habits, provide permanent waste infra, or sustain a clean-up alone.
Article Summary: Surendra Singh Choudhary, known as "Bittu Tabahi," is a 20-year-old college student from Madhya Pradesh. Bittu hogged international limelight for single- handedly cleaning up a stretch of Ajnar river in Rajgarh's Biaora. He says every time he cleans up the river, people dump garbage back into it.

Article Title: Cheered in Chhota Udepur, but Vadodara shuts stage to Muslim who played Lakshmana for 14 years
Article Text:
Abid Sheikh, an actor in Vadodara, was excluded from performing in Ram Leela due to his religion.





VADODARA: On Dussehra , Abid Sheikh drew applause in tribal Chhota Udepur for bringing the characters of Kevat and Meghnad alive on stage in a Ram Leela.In Vadodara, however, the city he calls home, the 39-year-old was unable to perform in the Ram Leela he had been associated with for nearly 14 years, after objections to his participation over his religion by right-wing groups.The contrast has left Sheikh, a science graduate who grew up fascinated by the Ramayana, grappling with an unexpected rejection from a tradition that had become an integral part of his life.For years, Sheikh played Laxman and Bharat in the Ram Leela organised by the North India Cultural Association (NICA) at Polo Ground during Dussehra. He learnt his dialogues, rehearsed for weeks and earned appreciation from audiences. His family, too, shared his commitment, giving up non-vegetarian food during the rehearsal period until the festival concluded.But the welcome he had long received on stage in Vadodara changed last year when some right-wing activists turned up during rehearsals and objected to his casting because he was a Muslim.“I played different roles in Ram Leela for around 14 years and was showered with love and appreciation by the audience.Last year, some activists suddenly turned up during rehearsals and objected to my casting because of my religion. I was shocked, as I never expected this,” Sheikh told TOI.He said the activists pressured the organisers to drop him. This year, he was not invited to perform in the Vadodara production.“Ram Leela had become a part of my life, but they did not want me anywhere near the stage,” he said.The rejection was particularly painful because his association with the epic began in childhood. After watching a cartoon based on the Ramayana, Sheikh developed a fascination for Laxman. An opportunity to perform in a school Ram Leela gave him his first taste of acting, and he continued playing characters from the epic for years.Shashikant Das, director, NICA, told TOI: “Sheikh is such a good actor and he is an ardent fan of Ramayan. He chants Hanuman Chalisa. But Bajrang Dal activists came last year and protested against his role. I argued and fought in Sheikh’s defence.”“But the management came under pressure. So, this time he wasn’t invited for the Ram Leela. It’s sad that we lost a good actor like him,” Das said and pointed out that those preparing the giant effigies of Ravana, Meghnad and Kumbhakarna at Polo Ground are also Muslim artists from Uttar Pradesh.
Article Summary: Abid Sheikh, an actor in Vadodara, was excluded from performing in Ram Leela due to his religion. Right-wing activists turned up during rehearsals and objected to his casting because he was a Muslim. He said the activists pressured the organisers to drop him.

Theauthor Bharat Muni takes the stage with his 100 children to seek Brahma’s permission to create theatre. Vedic chants fill the venue as a large 3D image of Shiva appears in the background. Dancers perform, and hymns are sung. Suddenly, the celebration comes to a standstill. The fourth wall breaks as a group of young people enter the stage, expressing their reluctance to participate in the drama.The opening is followed by a battle scene between Indra and the demons. Indra’s elaborate costume, his weaponand his majestic white elephant, Airavat, establish his power and grandeur. The intricately crafted costumes, with Indra brandishing his, make for an arresting visual.is visually stunning, with the stagecraft complementing its costumes. However, the somewhat chaotic setting and abrupt transitions come at the cost of narrative clarity.The battle sequences, props and the demons are among the production’s highlights. Indra’s entrance on Airavat, flanked byand dancers, steals the show. The attention to detail is remarkable, especially with regard to the characters of Airavat and Vasuki.Vasuki’s length as it coils around the mountain is impressive to behold. Depicting the churning of the ocean on a stage is a difficult feat to pull off, but the NSD repertory rises to the challenge.However, the play-within-a-play, a narrative technique used in works from Shakespeare to the, could have been more effective. The narrative framing of Bharat Muni’s story and its link to the mythological story feel uneven in parts, preventing the two from coming together seamlessly to tell a larger tale.However, whatlacked in storytelling, it made up for in the costume, music and acting departments. The choreography of the demons, their entry from beneath the stage, followed by their introduction through rhythmic movements and chants, was almost hypnotic. Yet the drama would have felt more complete had it been accompanied by more coherent storytelling.The production’s idea of using atale to underscore the modern crises that plague our world fails to land convincingly.-Anvita Singh

Article Title: Mumbai-bound traffic hit after hatchback catches fire on Vashi Creek bridge
Article Text:
The driver immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine.





NAVI MUMBAI: Vehicular traffic from Navi Mumbai towards Mumbai was disrupted for around 30 minutes after a hatchback caught fire while crossing the Vashi Creek Bridge on Friday at around 7.30pm.The driver escaped unhurt. He immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine. However, the fire soon engulfed the entire vehicle, leaving it completely charred.Vashi traffic police alerted the Vashi fire brigade, which reached the spot within 15 minutes. The charred vehicle was later towed away by a crane, following which traffic movement returned to normal.Sunil Kadam, senior inspector of the Vashi traffic unit, said the driver was identified as Sumit Bhikaji Kadam.“At around 7.45pm, we received a call from one Rahul, whose full name is not known, informing us that a car had caught fire on the Mumbai-bound lane of the Vashi Creek Bridge,” said AV Sisode, the on-duty fireman at Vashi fire station.“In the meantime, we also received a call from the Vashi traffic police and immediately rushed to the spot with a fire tender. The Mumbai fire brigade team had also reached the spot as there was some confusion over the jurisdiction,” Sisode said.The fire was subsequently extinguished, and the Vashi fire brigade team returned to the station at around 8.30pm.
Article Summary: The driver immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine. The fire soon engulfed the entire vehicle, leaving it completely charred. The charred vehicle was later towed away by a crane, following which traffic movement returned to normal.

Article Title: Mumbai-Goa highway crash: 30-year-old killed, 2 cousins injured after Honda City hits gate
Article Text:
30-year-old Akshay Kadam lost his life in a car accident after he lost control of his vehicle





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man driving his Honda City car was killed and his two friends, both paternal cousin brothers accompanying him were injured after the driver lost control over the wheels on the Mangaon-Mahad stretch of Mumbai-Goa highway after crossing Mangaon railway station and veering off the road crashed into the iron gate of an industrial unit.The fatal accident occured on Monday around 3 am, when the three friends had gone for dinner at a roadside food stall in Mangaon and were returning to their respective villages in Mahad taluka.The injured complainant stated in the FIR registered at Mangaon police station that the accused car driver and his cousin had consumed liquor before going for dinner.The deceased driver was identified as Akshay Arjun Kadam, a resident of Nandgaon, Mahad taluka. Those injured are Rohit Rajendra Dhadve (24), working as safety officer at Astriel Life Science Pvt Ltd in Mahad MIDC and his cousin Roshan Dilip Dhadve (24). Both residents of Kembhurli, Mahad taluka.Maruti Andhale, senior inspector of Mangaon said, "As the complainant Rohit Dhadve has stated in the FIR that the accused Akshay Kadam drove the car after consuming liquor along with his cousin Roshan, when they had meet near the bus stop, after which they went to Mangaon for dinner, the Motor Vehicle Act section for drunk driving will be invoked.However, as the accused car driver Akshay Kadam responsible for the car crash had died in the accident, a final closure 'Abated summary' report will be submitted before the Mangaon magistrate court. "As per the FIR by the complainant Rohit Dhadve, on Sept 28 around 1 am, when he was at home, his paternal cousin Roshan spoke to him over mobile, when Roshan's maternal cousin Akshay Kadam accompanying him told Rohit that he had come from Mumbai and asked him to meet near the bus stand at Kembhurli.When Rohit met them at the spot, Roshan and Akshay were consuming liquor inside Akshay's Honda City car. Thereafter, Akshay said, "Let's go to Mangaon to have food and the three of them went in the car with Akshay at the wheels."Roshan was sitting beside Akshay and Rohit on the rear seat. They reached Mangaon around 2 am, where they ate parathas at a road side food stall and took parcel of Khima Pav.Thereafter, they drove for 3 kms towards Indapur and took a U-turn to return to their villages in Mahad.After crossing 300 metres from Mangaon railway Station, Akshay lost control over the wheels and yanking off the road on the right side, he crashed into the iron gate of Sundha Steel Traders industrial unit.Rohit sustained injuries below his left eye, left hand and left knee. Akshay got stuck between the driver's seat and the door. Roshan's left leg was injured.Hearing the loud noice of the car crash, the locals gathered, removed the three injured out of the car and summoned 108 ambulance in which they were rushed to Mangaon sub-district hospital, where Akshay was declared brought dead on arrival.
Article Summary: Akshay Arjun Kadam, 30, lost his life in a car accident after he lost control of his vehicle on the Mumbai-Goa highway. His two friends, both paternal cousin brothers accompanying him were injured. The three friends had gone for dinner at a roadside food stall in Mangaon.

Article Title: Bengaluru artistes bring ‘Sri Devi Mahishasuramardini’ to life at Dombivli Navratri festival
Article Text:
Artistes from Bengaluru presented ‘Sri Devi Mahishasuramardini’, blending dance, drama, expressive acting and devotion to narrate the triumph of good over evil.





DOMBIVLI: A theatrical portrayal of Goddess Durga’s battle against demon Mahishasura offered Dombivli residents a glimpse into India’s traditional performing arts during the Sharadiya Navratri festival.Artistes from Bengaluru presented ‘Sri Devi Mahishasuramardini’, blending dance, drama, expressive acting and devotion to narrate the triumph of good over evil.The performance drew an enthusiastic response from the audience, with traditional costumes and dramatic sequences bringing the mythological tale of the goddess’s victory to life.The programme was organised as part of the Navratri celebrations hosted by the Dr Shrikant Shinde Foundation and Shri Navdurga Yuva Mandal at the DNC school grounds in Dombivli East.Kalyan MP Dr Shrikant Shinde, who attended the event, stressed the importance of preserving and promoting traditional art forms that reflect India's cultural heritage.“Artistic performances that preserve our culture and traditions are important. They need encouragement and support so that this rich heritage can be passed on to future generations,” Shinde said.The presentation centred on the story of Mahishasura, whose tyranny threatened the world until Goddess Durga took the form of Mahishasuramardini to defeat him.Through a combination of theatrical expression, dance and devotional elements, the Bengaluru artistes depicted the goddess’s strength and the victory of righteousness over evil.Organisers said the festival seeks to go beyond religious rituals by providing a platform for India's diverse cultural and spiritual traditions. Alongside devotional activities, the programme features performances showcasing different forms of traditional art.At a time when modern entertainment platforms are increasingly popular, such performances offer an opportunity to introduce younger audiences to India's mythological stories and traditional artistic expressions.They also help preserve cultural practices that have been passed down through generations.The Navratri festival has included a range of religious and cultural programmes, including the Navkundatmak Sahasrachandi Mahayag, Haripath, bhajan sessions and devotional music.The organisers have sought to combine religious observances with cultural activities to give visitors a wider experience of the festival.The ‘Sri Devi Mahishasuramardini’ presentation added a distinctive dimension to this year's celebrations, highlighting the role of traditional theatre in keeping India's mythological narratives and performing arts alive.
Article Summary: Bengaluru artistes presented ‘Sri Devi Mahishasuramardini’, blending dance, drama, expressive acting and devotion to narrate the triumph of good over evil. The performance drew an enthusiastic response from the audience, with traditional costumes and dramatic sequences bringing the mythological tale to life.

Article Title: 99-year-old Pune man survives fall that could’ve paralysed him, thanks to ‘daily walks’
Article Text:
The elderly man was discharged from hospital after spine surgery within weeks of the fall. Doctors credited his fitness for the speedy recovery

Pune

:

TOI





A 99-year-old Pune resident survived a serious fall that could have left him bedridden or dependent on caregivers for life, thanks to an active lifestyle and timely spine surgery, his doctors have said. The fall had caused acute nerve compression in the man’s lumbar spine, resulting in severe pain and hampered movement. But because he was fit, doctors were able to intervene with surgery - not always possible in patients of this age.“Age is indeed an important consideration, but it should not be the only factor guiding the decision. This patient led an independent life before the incident, and our focus was to relieve the nerve compression and help him regain his mobility. His early recovery was encouraging,” said Dr Tushar Deore, spine surgeon at Sahyadri Super Speciality Hospital, who led the surgery..The man suffered the fall in the first week of Aug. His surgery was over by Oct 5. Dr Deore said his patient started walking two days later. By day three, his pain had vanished and by Oct 8, the 99-year-old man was out of hospital.He toldthat even at 99 he was “out walking every day” to his shop. “I never used my age as an excuse and continued taking care of my health,” the man said, adding that the improvement in mobility “is an important step towards returning to my usual routine”.Dr Deore said considering the patient’s age, overall health and functional capacity the medical team assessed potential benefits and risks of surgical intervention before proceeding with treatment. He said: “The treatment aimed to relieve the pressure on the affected nerves and improve the patient’s mobility. Managing a patient at an advanced age requires careful preoperative assessment, appropriate anaesthesia management and close monitoring during recovery. In this case, the surgical and anaesthesia teams worked alongside the postoperative care and physiotherapy teams to support the patient’s recovery and early mobilisation.”Postoperative rehabilitation is particularly important for older adults, as prolonged immobility can affect muscle strength, balance and the ability to perform routine activities. Early mobilisation, when medically appropriate, along with monitoring and physiotherapy, can support recovery and help patients work towards regaining their independence, added Dr Deore.He said the case highlights the importance of “individualized” treatment planning for elderly patients with spinal conditions. While surgery may not be appropriate for everyone, a comprehensive assessment can help determine whether an intervention is likely to improve comfort, mobility and quality of life, he said.
Article Summary: The 99-year-old Pune resident survived a serious fall that could have left him bedridden or dependent on caregivers for life. The fall had caused acute nerve compression in the man’s lumbar spine, resulting in severe pain and hampered movement. But because he was fit, doctors were able to intervene with surgery.

Article Title: Motorcycle-borne man snatches gold chain worth Rs3 lakh in Pune
Article Text:
Representative image

Pune:





A motorcycle-borne man allegedly snatched a 70-year-old woman’s gold chain worth Rs3 lakh around 9 am on Tuesday in Aundh.The woman, a homemaker from Aundh, lodged a complaint at Chatushrungi police station later on Tuesday.Sub-inspector Aniket Pote of Chatushrungi police station said, “The complainant had gone to a laughter club for senior citizens. After attending the club, she was walking back towards her flat.”“After crossing the main road, when she reached a bylane leading to her residential society, a motorcycle rider came from behind and snatched her gold chain worth Rs3 lakh. The complainant raised an alarm, but by then, the suspect had sped away towards Baner. We are examining CCTV footage from the spot and trying to ascertain the motorcycle’s registration number,” Pote said.

The woman, a homemaker from Aundh, lodged a complaint at Chatushrungi police station later on Tuesday. Article Title: Lucknow Cafe Owner Death: 11th Floor Clue, CCTV Trail End UP-Nepal-Nagpur Great Escape; Live-In Partner Shraddha Dubey,2 Aides Nabbed
Article Text:
Accused Shraddha Dubey, driver Danish and Rashmi Dubey

Nagpur:





Eleven days after a 27-year-old Lucknow cafe owner, Shiva Sharma , died after falling off the fourth floor of an upscale apartment in the Uttar Pradesh capital, a joint team of Nagpur crime branch and Lucknow police arrested Sharma’s live-in partner, Shraddha Dubey, her sister Rashmi Dubey and their driver Adil from Chinchbhuvan here on Tuesday.Clad in a burqa, influencer-model Shraddha Dubey’s roller-coaster run from Lucknow to Agra to Nepal to Nagpur finally ended after an ‘11th floor’ clue provided by the getaway vehicle’s driver along with an e-rickshaw’s CCTV trail of 250 cameras.After searching 12 locations with internet-based location inputs and CCTV footage, police traced the trio to a rented flat on the 11th floor of an apartment in Chinchbhuvan on Nagpur outskirts. The mission kicked off after Lucknow police commissioner made a call to Nagpur commissioner Vishwas Nangare Patil on Monday evening and shared the registration number and location details of the vehicle used by suspects.Crime Branch teams began tracking their movements and checking possible hideouts across the city, said DCP crime Deepak Aggarwal.During questioning, the car driver from Uttar Pradesh reportedly told investigators the trio had travelled in an e-rickshaw after reaching the Ganeshpeth area.He also provided a crucial lead on a discussion involving the ‘11th floor’, which he overheard. This information helped investigators narrow the search.Police teams searched 12 locations, including Gaddigodam and Chinchbhuvan, while tracking the suspects on CCTV and GPS inputs. “Investigators examined footage from around 250 cameras to establish the e-rickshaw’s route,” said ACP Vaibhav Jadhav, adding three crime branch teams were formed. “An Uttar Pradesh police team reached Monday and another touched down on Wednesday.The vehicle was last traced on CCTV in Chinchbhuvan, helping police identify the apartment where the trio was hiding. Investigators also found that Shraddha’s driver and co-accused, Adil, was using his mobile phone to make bookings and coordinate movements.Shraddha and Rashmi allegedly relied on the driver’s phone instead of using their own devices, making the digital trail an important part of the investigation, said a source.After zeroing in on the 11-storied flat Chinchbhuvan bridge, police kept the premises under surveillance for nearly 24 hours. A team from Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force (STF) later joined the operation, and the three suspects were taken into custody.Shraddha, who had been on the run for 10 days, moving between Nepal, Agra, Lucknow and Kanpur before reaching Nagpur, wore a burqa to conceal her identity. She had also released a video claiming Sharma had died by suicide.
Article Summary: Shraddha Dubey had been on the run for 10 days, moving between Nepal, Agra, Lucknow and Kanpur. She wore a burqa to conceal her identity. She had also released a video claiming Sharma had died by suicide.

Article Title: Mental hospital inmate defeats cancer, reunites with father on Dussehra
Article Text:
Nagpur:





A woman who battled cancer while struggling with mental health issues was reunited with her father after 10 years on Tuesday, marking a heartwarming Dussehra milestone for the staff of the Regional Mental Hospital. Nanda (name changed), believed to be from Wardha, had spent several years moving between rescue agencies, NGOs and shelter homes before being admitted to the Regional Mental Hospital in Nagpur on March 19, 2024, through the govt-run Priyadarshini women’s hostel. With no clear family details, tracing her home proved challenging.She was 39 at the time. During routine medical examinations, doctors diagnosed her with cancer on Nov 29, 2024. She was shifted to Government Medical College and Hospital (GMCH), where chemotherapy and other treatment began. By July 2025, however, the cost of continuing treatment had become a major concern.With no Aadhaar or ration card and her family still untraceable, accessing financial assistance under the Mahatma Jyotiba Phule Jan Arogya Yojana became difficult. Hospital staff, however, continued exploring ways to ensure that her treatment was not interrupted.Social service superintendent Kunda Katkhaye Bidkar took the lead in tracing Nanda’s family. With help from Wardha district police patils Nitesh Bidkar and Babita Ghugare, the team eventually located her father.Initially, he expressed his inability to take her back because of financial and family difficulties. Bidkar continued counselling him until he agreed to visit his daughter. On August 7, 2025, he finally reached the hospital and met her after a decade.“The reunion also helped the hospital complete Nanda’s documentation, obtain an Ayushman Bharat card and register her under the state health scheme,” Bidkar said.With the documentation hurdles addressed, Nanda’s treatment resumed. Doctors, nurses and support staff provided medical care, counselling, food and emotional support.The latest cancer-related test reports came back negative on the eve of Vijayadashami, bringing immense relief to the hospital team. “This victory is of the mental hospital staffers against cancer and also of Nanda’s, as she had shown much mental resilience,” Bidkar said.Staff members celebrated the family reunion and the reassuring test results by presenting Nanda with flowers and sweets.
Article Summary: Nanda (name changed) had spent several years moving between rescue agencies, NGOs and shelter homes. She was admitted to the Regional Mental Hospital in Nagpur on March 19, 2024, through the govt-run Priyadarshini women’s hostel. With no clear family details, tracing her home proved challenging.

Article Title: Chennai metro phase 2 services to start at 6am from tomorrow
Article Text:
Chennai Metro Rail Ltd will begin operations for the Phase-2 Yellow Line at an earlier time of 6am





CHENNAI: Chennai Metro Rail Ltd (CMRL) will advance the services on the Phase-2 Yellow Line to 6am from Oct 23, following commuter feedback. Services on the 15km Corridor-4 stretch between Poonamallee Bypass and Vadapalani will operate from 6am to 9pm in both directions.Currently, services begin at 7am. The revised timings are intended to make early-morning travel towards Vadapalani and Poonamallee more convenient.From Monday to Saturday, trains will run every 10 minutes during peak hours — 8am to 11am and 5pm to 8pm. During non-peak hours, services will operate every 15 minutes, between 6am and 8am, 11am and 5pm, and 8pm and 9pm.
Article Summary: Chennai Metro Rail Ltd will advance the services on the Phase-2 Yellow Line to 6am from Oct 23, following commuter feedback. Services on the 15km Corridor-4 stretch between Poonamallee Bypass and Vadapalani will operate from 6am to 9pm in both directions.
